terms.meaning: An economic activity of producing goods and services and getting them to consumers.
The part of business concerned with buying and selling goods.
Trade inside a country, through retailers and wholesalers.
Buying from one country in order to sell to others. Singapore is the best example.
Honest, fair ways of doing business, with only a reasonable profit.
Services that remove obstacles between producer and consumer.

items.name: Economic objectives
items.formula: A reasonable profit that covers costs, and supplying what consumers need.
items.example: It uses new techniques and tells people through advertisement.

items.name: Social objectives
items.formula: Jobs at fair wages, paying taxes, and welfare work.
items.example: Starting schools, hospitals and public gardens.

items.name: Retailers
items.formula: Buy from wholesalers and sell to consumers, as the last link.
items.example: They also store goods, give credit and suggest alternatives.

items.name: Hawkers and peddlers
items.formula: Hawkers carry goods on their heads, usually one or two kinds. Peddlers use wheeled carts, with more kinds.

items.name: Street traders and shandy sellers
items.formula: Street traders sell on pavements. Shandy sellers come to weekly markets.
items.example: Villagers bring what they grow and buy their needs with the money.

items.name: Wholesalers
items.formula: Buy in large quantities from producers and sell in small quantities to retailers.
items.example: They give credit, storage and market news.

items.name: Three types of foreign trade
items.formula: Import: buying from other countries. Export: selling to them. Entrepot: buying in order to resell.
items.example: Singapore and Middle East countries do entrepot trade.

items.name: Why countries need foreign trade
items.formula: No country has all natural resources.
items.example: Those with extra export and those short of something import.

items.name: Primary industries
items.formula: Genetic: raising crops and animals (dairy, poultry). Extractive: taking materials from the earth (mining, oil).

items.name: Secondary industries
items.formula: Manufacturing: raw material to finished goods (sugarcane to sugar). Construction: roads, canals and bridges.

items.name: Cottage and small scale industries
items.formula: Cottage: at home with family, for local markets (pottery, carpentry). Small scale: in sheds, with power and machines.
items.example: Small scale goods: soaps, fans, bicycles.

groups.title: Aids to trade and fair practice

items.name: Which service removes which hindrance
items.formula: Place: transport. Finance: banks. Loss: insurance. Time: storage. Knowledge: advertisement.
items.example: Warehouses with cold storage solve the time problem.

items.name: Unethical business practices
items.formula: Adulteration, overcharging, false weights, hoarding and black marketing.
items.example: They make people suffer and should be avoided.

items.name: Government steps for fair business
items.formula: Public Distribution System, Bureau of Indian Standards, ISI and AGMARK marks.
items.example: Also Janatha bazaars, co-operative societies and printing the MRP.

mistakes.text: The aim of business isn't just profit: it is reasonable profit plus social objectives.
Import is buying and export is selling. In entrepot trade the goods are bought to be sold abroad again.
Genetic industries grow living things and can renew them. Extractive ones can't be renewed.
